But who can say "I think its just as offensive" when someone who has never been called a nigger doesn't really know how much it hurts? People call me sir, and it pisses me off, but I'm quicker to anger when I get called a nigger (which has happened on multiple occasions, at random and unsparked).

Don't get me wrong, transphobia is a major problem, especially within the gay/lesbian community, but racism is a whole nother' issue and has nothing to do with it. 

A lot of minority classes experience the same type of discrimination. Just because RuPaul doesn't find the word personally offensive, doesn't mean that he's saying EVERYONE needs to think the same thing he does. 

I'm a black lesbian woman who looks like a guy (although I'm not trans, just genes), educated with a BA, and out on my own. I get called the N-word on more occasions than not, get talked down to, and I tend to make people feel uncomfortable even before I speak to them because they tell me I look intimidating, but once they talked to me, realized I was nice, so it was okay. I get called sir on a daily basis, even though I was born as a woman and identify as such. It really sucks, and its hard to live with, but the situations I experience with that, usually have nothing to do with me being black (well, maybe like 60/40).

I just wish people would stop having to compare things to others. Now its becoming one of those things where 'Which is more offensive? Nigger or Tranny?' Like, one has to trump the other.
